result.rationale: The diff shows groups_controller.rb#members: `offset = params[:offset].to_i` with no lower clamp, then `members.limit(limit).offset(offset)`. The Ember client clamps (`Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0)` in group.js findMembers), but the public endpoint accepts arbitrary negative offsets, and Rails' .offset() with a negative value raises ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid, yielding a 500. The controller code shown has no guard, so the mechanism is verifiable from the diff.

judged_text: offset = params[:offset].to_i is passed to .offset() with no lower clamp, so a client-supplied negative offset reaches PostgreSQL as OFFSET -n. GET /groups/<name>/members.json?offset=-1 raises 'OFFSET must not be negative' (ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid) and returns an HTML 500 on this public endpoint instead of a 4xx; the Ember client clamps its own offset, but any API consumer sending a negative value gets a 500.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then calls `group.users...offset(offset)` with no validation/clamp (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb). A client can supply `offset=-1`, which will be passed through to ActiveRecord/PostgreSQL as a negative OFFSET and can raise an error (server 500) on this public endpoint. The Ember client clamping doesn’t protect other API consumers.
